messages.text: For Saturday, I put you at one place setting unless you tell me different. Tasha is bringing the folding chairs.
One is right. I will bring the bakery cookies and come straight from my apartment.
Good. I also found that old Queens photo with Elaine in the blue coat. Do you want it or should I leave it in the envelope?
Leave it in the envelope for now. Nice memory, but I do not need it out on the shelf.
Uncle Fredick, do you still have that envelope with Grandma's Savannah address and the church card? I want to show Mom before Saturday.
Uncle Fred, did you see the housing questionnaire for the June city races? I sent the link in the family chat.
Yes. I put it with the scanned photos and the 1940 sheet. I will bring copies, not the originals.
I saved it. I want to read the answers side by side with the Board packet before I mark anything.
Good. Also Mom said you already volunteered for the baked thing again, so nobody is fighting over dessert.
Of course you made homework out of it 😂 Just don't let the slick mailers fool you.
Bakery on Nostrand opens at 8. I will pick up the pound cake and keep the papers flat in the hard folder.
Mailers go in one pile, records in another. Good ideas matter, but so does whether someone can run an office.
Unc, when you do your monthly sheet, do you list every automatic pull separate or just one total?
Separate. Rent, ConEd, phone, Medicare supplement, dental payment. Then I match them against the consulting deposit and the retirement deposit.
That is cleaner. I keep forgetting little charges.
The fewer moving parts, the better. I pay the card after the statement closes so April starts at zero.
You got MSG on? Knicks down 6 already.
I have it on. One Brooklyn lager, a bowl of pretzels, and I am staying with the broadcast until they stop turning it over.
Unc that sounds calmer than my place. Guys here keep running to the stoop every timeout.
That is why I watch at home. Halftime window cracked, then seltzer after the bottle is done.
The Weeksville notice I mentioned is up now. The opening has archive photos, planning maps, and oral recordings from Crown Heights.
Send it over. I still have those HOLC map screenshots from the library site, so that might fit together.
I thought of you because the wall text is supposed to connect streets, mortgages, and family movement without making it feel like a textbook.
That sounds worth the train ride. I will mark Saturday and bring the small camera.
Your hallway photo with the radiator pipes made me think of the old apartment buildings around Fulton. Was that near where you and Denise grew up?
A few blocks from the place on Halsey where we were teenagers. Dad would notice every bad valve and loose stair rail before anyone else.
That explains the eye for repair details. Bring that print Friday; I want to compare it with the stairwell shot.
The frame you put up this afternoon has a good quietness to it. I would trim a little from the left edge.
I almost did not put that one anywhere. The color version made the storefront sign too loud.
Good instinct. The man in the doorway is the real center, not the sign.
I may leave it up for a bit. I only opened Instagram to answer your note and saw Denise had tagged me in Marcus's birthday album.
Uncle Fredick, do you still have that phone photo from the summer everyone was walking past Grand Army Plaza? The one with the cardboard signs.
I have one or two buried in the old folder. I only went that afternoon, so there are not many.
Uncle Fredick, the community board agenda has that item about public complaint files and the 911 pilot. Are you going or just watching online?
Uncle Fred, do you remember what Grandma used to play from the front room when the windows were open? Mom says you always know the song names.
Uncle Fred, for the family tree page, was Granddad's side still Georgia and Grandma's people South Carolina?
Watching online. I want to hear whether they keep a written trail when the same badge number keeps coming up.
Some days it was Marvin Gaye drifting out from one apartment, then James Brown from another before the block even cooled down.
Yes. Daddy always said outside Savannah, and Mama's people near Charleston before they came north.
That is enough. I am making a little family timeline, not asking you to sign up for weekly meetings with me lol.
And you and Mom were on Macon Street then, right? I want the caption right.
Good, because my part was mostly showing up once, reading, voting, and talking with you all at Denise's table.
That is exactly the part people skip. Also the proposal says counselors ride first for some calls, not a squad car.
That is exactly the kind of detail I need. Was that before or after the Sunday clothes and big dinner routine?
Macon, then Halsey. Same blocks where Mrs. Baptiste sent over patties and the church ladies watched everybody's children.
Good. Some doors need calm voices before uniforms. I learned that from both sides of a store counter.
Same season of life. Pressed shirt, polished shoes, handclaps still in my head, then somebody's radio taking over the evening.
You remember when payroll tried to shave those closing minutes off the stock crew?
I remember being the one with the salary badge and still telling them to fix the time sheets. Wrong is wrong.
And then you made the new schedule chart so nobody missed breaks. Store manager hated that chart.
He hated that it made the promise visible. Same thing with city programs: don't announce something nice if the counter staff cannot actually run it.
Still good for diner coffee at 11? I remember you said Friday mornings were clean unless one of those store owners starts calling.
Still good. I finished the inventory notes for Mr. Alvarez last night and told the bakery I am not adding a fifth afternoon this week.
Good. Three places can already make a man feel like he has ten bosses.
Exactly why I keep the calendar tight. About 22 hours is enough when the paperwork follows me home.
Unc, quick question. Closing screen froze after the Z-read and the receipt printer kicked out blanks. Manager also wants two people moved off Saturday night.
Do the printer power cycle first, then check if the drawer count posted before you touch anything else. For Saturday, move the stronger opener later and write down who approved it.
Got it. You still want me to export the day file instead of typing totals?
Yes. Send the CSV into one sheet with columns for voids, returns, hours, and who closed. Hand-typed totals always come back to bite somebody.
The Park Slope opening is Thursday at 6. Small room, good prints, no speeches if we arrive after the first wave.
That sounds workable. I can meet at 6:25, look through the back wall first, then one coffee nearby.
Very specific, as usual. I will send the exhibit link so you can inspect the list beforehand.
Send it. If the cafe is crowded, I may just walk you to 7th Avenue and head back.
Did the office take your check already? You sounded tight when we talked Sunday.
They took it Tuesday. After that clears, I have to keep the rest of March plain.
Please do not start talking yourself into packing boxes over one bad month.
No boxes. Broker fee, movers, deposits, all those stairs again. Staying quiet here is cheaper on my knees and my account.
Unc, can I have a package sent to you Tuesday? My lobby loses boxes.
Uncle Fred, when you set up those automatic transfers, did you keep them all at one bank or split them up?
Tuesday works if it comes after 3. I need to be there to buzz it up; nobody else will catch the door.
Split. Checking pays bills, one bucket is plain bank money, and the market stuff sits elsewhere so I do not touch it for a broken tire or a dentist surprise.
Cool. I will put your name and the Brooklyn address.
Makes sense. I got hit with a $400 car thing today and I am trying not to make it worse.
Use the small front closet if I step out for coffee. The back room is covered in clamps and invoice folders again.
For that amount, I would pay it clean if the bank bucket is there. In a crowded week, I have used the card and paid it right back when the invoice money landed.
Uncle Fredick, are you still coming by for the exhibit talk tomorrow? I can save you a seat.
I may skip this one. I am moving a few things around after that mouth-office quote, and my old walking pair has one more week in it.
One more week sounds like your famous "temporary" fixes 😂. Send me the exhibit link anyway?
I will. I put the pair in next month's column, after the big chair deposit clears.
Uncle Fredick, I sent that rent thread earlier but ignore it tonight if it gets your mind running.
I saw the first two posts and stopped. I am trying to leave those apps alone once the dishes are done.
Fair. Also Denise said you bought the big cheese block again, so put half in the freezer before midnight finds you.
Already wrapped it. Long invoices today had me walking to the kitchen every hour.
Still good for coffee Friday? Diner on 18th, same booth if they do not give it away.
Yes. I may skip the second cup there. Bought beans yesterday and that little bag was 17.25.
SEVENTEEN for beans. Better taste like it knows your name.
I put it in the sheet with the salmon and oil. Also sent one more note to Mercer about the February invoice before I touch anything extra.
I will be around after church. Six-thirty still good for you?
Before I forget on our call, did you put Dr. Patel's March visit on the calendar?
Yes, I kept that spot open. I want to hear how Marcus's new manager handled the schedule mess.
Yes, Thursday morning. Just the usual check-in, and I wrote down the home readings he asked for.
He may text you himself. Tasha also found one more question about Grandma's move north, so have your memory ready.
Good. Bring the pill bottle too, even if nothing changed. You know how they ask.
Tell them both I am available. Also, do you still have the small brass one on the blue ring?
Already in the bag with my card and glasses.
You sounded a little stiff on the phone. Did you do those stretches before running around yesterday?
Not enough. I got there late and went straight onto the court.
Fredick. Eat something before you take anything from that little bottle, please.
I did. Toast first, then just one. I am taking the stairs slow today.
I am home after church. Call when you finish dinner, same as usual.
Around 7:15. I started typing something earlier and stopped. Better to talk it through with you.
Did you ever hear back from Dr. Kline's office about that pharmacy appointment?
Before our call, can you show me that freeze-the-top-row thing you were telling me about? My office list is a mess.
Portal reply came in. He said I can do the arm visit this month, but I am checking the city page too.
I can. I watched a short clip on it last night and copied the steps into that old blue notebook from BMCC.
Good. You know I would rather hear your voice than guess what is going on from a few sentences.
I know. Calvin heard a little Friday, but I wanted your read before I make any calls tomorrow.
You still have those notebooks? Bring one Sunday if you come to Queens. I remember you carrying them on the train after work.
Good. Please do not let Tasha's comment thread make you second-guess a doctor's note.
It won't. I saved the real links and skipped the bottle-selling video under it.
Only the useful ones. The rest are in a box with the old records and tuition receipts.
You sounded wound up after church today. Did you eat something real?
I ate. Bills are still on the table, but I put on the soft Coltrane side and stopped touching the envelopes for a while.
Good. Leave those papers alone tonight if you can. Call me after the last song if you still feel tight.
I will. The lamp is low and I am just sitting with it.
You still got that clamp set? I need one for a cabinet door at my place.
Yes. I am using two tonight on that slim hallway piece, but the small ones are free after 7.
No rush. You buying new hardware for it?
Only if the old pulls look foolish after cleaning. A sound piece does not need jewelry.
Unc, they want me to move from dispatch sheets into assistant lead. More keys, more calls, same messy weekends.
Ask what changes in writing. When I took the Brooklyn spot, the extra keys mattered more than the title on the badge.
So don't get dazzled by the new name if the pay and schedule stay vague.
Exactly. A steady shop with real authority can carry you farther than a shiny route you don't control.
The light near the library steps should be good by 11:00. Bring the small camera if you come.
I may walk over. I have looked at the same dental estimate four times and need to get away from the kitchen table.
Then walk over. You can compare shadows instead of columns for an hour.
That sounds better. I put Coltrane on and I am putting the papers in the drawer until noon.
The opening ends at five. Shall we get something near Court Street afterward?
I can sit for coffee, but I am passing on a full plate out. I have a pot on the stove and some mint that needs trimming.
Coffee is fine. Bring the photograph from the Fulton stop if you printed it.
Will do. I left enough soup for later, so no need for me to chase dinner.
The Brooklyn Botanic garden has a small print show with raked gravel, temple gates, and narrow lanes. You would study every shadow.
That is exactly the sort of frame I keep saving. Stone paths, worn wood, hand tools in shop windows, no rushing from stop to stop.
Then pick one afternoon for the camera and one morning for a museum, not twelve perfect stops on a spreadsheet.
I know. Last night I had three airline tabs open and still ended up adding notes about train exits instead of choosing dates.
The old Kings County complex has some wonderful exterior lines. If we walk by Wednesday, bring that small camera.
Funny timing. I was just looking at a form where that name may need to be written exactly right.
Then we can make it practical and visual. Nostrand first, then coffee if your knees behave.
That route works. I know those blocks better than most maps do.
Uncle Fred, Marcus said you fixed that delivery-board mess in one visit. You ever think about doing a little Saturday thing for newer supervisors?
Only if they bring real examples. I do better with schedules, invoices, and where boxes actually pile up.
That is exactly what people need. Also please book Kyoto before you make twelve more spreadsheets about it 😄
The fare alert is saved. I am still keeping two blank weekdays most weeks, so I have no excuse.
The light on 5th Avenue looked good this morning. Did your 8:30 crowd take that route?
We stayed closer to the center today. Wind was cutting across the avenue, but I got one decent shot near the bakery gate.
Send it when you have a chance. A tighter crop may make the gate pattern stronger.
I will. Also carried home two basil starts from JoAnn, so the balcony is getting crowded again.
Happy 64th, Freddie. Mama would have called before sunrise and told the whole story again.
She never let March 12 pass quietly. I can still hear her correcting everybody on the details.
Come to Queens Sunday if you feel up to it. No big fuss, just cake and the usual family noise.
Sunday is fine. I will take the train and bring those old envelopes you asked about.
Did you finish that health plan renewal? Do not leave it for the last minute, Fredick.
I uploaded the forms this afternoon. Same Marketplace plan, higher premium, of course.
I know you like being on your own schedule, but please keep a cushion for that and the taxes.
I am. February was $4,800 before the tax bucket, so March bills are covered if the late invoice comes in.
You still got that little step counter thing? Mine keeps yelling at me after dispatch days.
Mine yelled by 3 pm. Too many hours in the chair, so I walked the long way to the pharmacy.
Long way is good. Knicks at 8 if you are watching.
I will watch the game and keep the crackers in the cabinet. No scrolling through the front-page apps after the final buzzer.
Unc, Mom asked if you still want me to carry that storage bin up Saturday. The one with the photo sleeves and Dad's blue folder?
Yes, please. My knee is not doing that staircase twice. Put the blue folder on top so it does not get crushed.
Got it. And are you making the tray or buying this time? I need to know before I stop at BJ's.
I am making the macaroni and cheese Friday night. If you can grab the foil lids, that helps.
Coffee still 10:30? Diner has those flyers by the register again.
Yes. Bring the one with the council questionnaire if it is still there. I want to compare it with the Tribune list.
Still on for 18th Avenue coffee? I can do 9:30. NO LATE-INVOICE TALK until after eggs.
9:30 works. I made a short sheet last night so I do not keep opening the same two emails.
You and your comparison charts. I just want somebody who fixes trash pickup and doesn't talk in clouds.
Good. Bring the sheet, not the whole folder. And leave the cable news alone before you get here.
That is part of my chart. Promises are easy; departments still have to function Monday morning.
Already took the long way around the block. Folder stays home.
Coffee still 10:30? Bring the little black notebook if you want me to look at those fare columns. NO TWENTY-TAB BUSINESS at the table.
Coffee at 10 still? I brought that ugly sales file from Linda's place. The onions are disappearing on paper again.
Still coming. If she has the item movement printout and the last order sheet, I can match them before the coffee gets cold.
10:30 works. I only printed two pages: flights through Haneda or Kansai, plus a list of places close enough to walk between.
You and those little colored tabs. Thirty rows and suddenly everybody confesses.
Diner tomorrow? Same booth if the coffee machine has not retired before us.
Only if the receiving dates and return slips are in there. Otherwise it is just pretty guessing.
Tomorrow works. 9:30 to 10:20 is best; I have two calls to return before lunch.
Good. If the day has old streets, a museum, and time to take pictures, that is a day. You are not managing a loading dock overseas.
Fair. I keep trying to solve every sign, ticket window, and train change before I even put money down.
You time coffee like a train schedule. I will be there.
Bring the invoice story. I want to hear it, but I am keeping the rest of the morning clear.
Coffee next Friday still good? I found that old photo from the Flatbush stockroom. You with the clipboard like you owned the place.
I remember that week. Two trucks late, three people out, and Mr. Hanley still pushing me about that buyer-training thing downtown.
You stayed with us and fixed the mess. Some of us still benefited, believe it or not.
That mess taught me the work people still pay me to look at now: schedules, shrink, deliveries, all of it.
Coffee tomorrow or you saving your voice for the Yankee game?
Coffee still works. I will be home by first pitch with one bottle from the corner and the radio on low.
ONE bottle. You make a wild night sound like inventory control.
Inventory control kept us employed. Besides, I do not need anything stronger than a close ninth inning.
Unc, quick question. If my supervisor changes the Saturday board after posting it, should I ask for it in writing?
Yes. Keep it short and polite. A text or email is enough if it has the date on it.
Got it. Ma said you two are doing your call Sunday, so I can give her the update to pass along.
Send it to me too. I told her to check that blue-ring copy before the month gets too busy.
The print shop wrote back. Your two 11x14 prints would be $86 before framing. I know you were being careful with March expenses.
Thank you. I can do the prints, but I am waiting until after I mark the March sheet. I like seeing the six lines of regular bills covered before I add extras.
That is very you, Fredick. Sensible, if a little stern with yourself.
The stern part keeps me from raiding the Vanguard and Schwab side for every nice-looking thing.
The Weeksville exhibit has a small listening alcove. You might like the street recordings more than the photographs, honestly.
If there is an organ line, a room answering a lead voice, or somebody keeping time with their palms, I will probably stand there too long.
Then I will warn the guard in advance. Also, bring that Bed-Stuy ear of yours; one panel mentions radios carrying through open windows.
That sound can put me right back on the block faster than any photograph.
The crop on the umbrella photograph is stronger if you let the curb line breathe.
I see it now. I am going to look again after dinner with the tenor record on low.
That may help. Your night edits usually have more patience than the afternoon ones.
Especially when I start with the old standards side and do not rush the first pass.
I found that Bed-Stuy oral history link and can stop by Sunday after the exhibit if you want to scan it together.
Come Sunday afternoon. I will move the sanding blocks off the scanner table and clear one chair.
One chair? Uncle Fredick, your place stays museum-neat except that project room 😂
That room earns its keep. Desk on one wall, tools on the other, and the monthly bills stacked between them.
Uncle Fred, did you find the photo of Grandma in that white uniform? Mom said it was from before I was born.
Uncle Fredick, Denise said you're coming Sunday. Should I bring anything or are you doing your usual kitchen magic? 🙂
I found one tucked behind Denise's class picture. Grandma had just come off a long shift and still made us sit straight for the camera.
Nothing fancy. I have linguine, a bunch of green leaves clipped this morning, and enough rice if Marcus shows hungry.
That sounds exactly like Mom's stories. Was that the Halsey apartment?
Yes, small front room, four of us squeezed in, but nobody left the table without being checked on.
Green leaves from your little rail setup?
Some from there, some from the store. I am keeping the receipt pile quiet this week.
Uncle Fred, sending you this article about Mrs. Alvarez's building on Fulton. Same block where Grandma used to shop. Wild.
Uncle Fred, did you ever finish that piece I sent about the old FHA map colors? The comments are a mess, but the source scans are good.
I read the scans, not the comments. The side-by-side with the 1940 census pages was more useful.
I read it. People her age should not have to learn new trains and new doctors because a notice came under the door.
That is exactly why I sent it to you 😂 Also the Schomburg page posted a walking tour clip from Harlem to Bed-Stuy.
Exactly. And everybody acts like it is just numbers on a spreadsheet.
Those numbers are why I look at my own renewal twice before I sleep.
Forward that clip. I want to compare it with the chapter I marked about rail lines and who landed near which blocks.
You see that new memo from the Avenue merchants group? Same old advice: call, wait, document EVERYTHING.
Documentation saved me more than once when I had to clear the sidewalk, handle a shoplifter, or explain why a young clerk got questioned.
Yep. Names, times, car number. Folks act like memory is enough.
Memory gets treated different depending who is standing there. Paper speaks more evenly.
Coffee after the game later, or you hiding in that apartment with sandpaper again?
Coffee at 3 works. I need one more pass on the legs first. If it wobbles in the hall, I will see it every morning.
That sounds like you. Plain and square before pretty.
Pretty can wait. I want it to hold keys, mail, and Denise's spare umbrella without pretending to be more than it is.
Coffee Friday still good? Same diner. I can do 10 if you are not waiting on anybody at the apartment.
Ten works. Nobody to work around here except the super checking the radiator.
Saw Elaine near 86th yesterday. She asked if you still carry that old Minolta. Friendly enough.
That sounds like her. Tell her the Minolta finally retired, but I appreciated the thought.
You still going to the courts this morning or sitting this one out?
Going to try a couple games. If the leg complains, I will leave early.
Bring the wrap. And don't skip the old-man warmup.
Already packed. Water, paddle, wrap, and that 200 mg bottle Denise keeps fussing about.
Unc, you know how to make the schedule sheet flag anyone over 40 hours? My boss sent it back again.
Send me a blank copy. I saved a video on conditional rules and will try it before lunch.
Appreciate it. You always explain it like those old office courses without making it sound fancy.
Those nights on Chambers Street were practical. Ledgers, payroll examples, inventory sheets. Same bones, newer buttons.
The Atlantic Avenue opening is Thursday at 6:30. Your stairwell photograph would fit the mood of that room.
Thursday works. I will bring the small print and skip putting the rough version up first.
Bring the tighter crop, not the wider one. And do not let Calvin be the only person who sees your work before it leaves your apartment.
Fair. You and Calvin get the preview committee, then Mr. Alvarez if he is still at the center Friday.
The negatives from Macon Street are wonderful. The storefront with the LP crates has the strongest composition.
That was Mr. Wilkes's place. I spent allowance money there before I knew what a light meter was.
The church hats in the background give the frame such rhythm. May I suggest printing that one larger?
Maybe 8x10. Denise will laugh because half those ladies corrected us from porch to porch.
The library exhibit includes several 2020 Brooklyn street photographs. Your Grand Army Plaza image would sit well beside them, especially if you crop out the traffic light.
I will send the tighter crop. That day was more walking than photographing for me.
That may be why the frame works. It is observant without trying to be grand.
That sounds about right. I tend to show up quietly, give a little when I can, then go back to my regular routines.
Uncle Fred, did you see the old Fulton Mall thread I sent you? Folks are dropping family photos in the comments.
Uncle Fred, I sent you that thread because people were arguing hard in there. Did you read it?
I saw it this morning. I did not join in, but I saved the one with the old shoe store.
I looked, then went to Dr. Kline's portal and the CDC page. The thread got loud fast.
Fair. Some of those replies were doing too much, especially the guy linking his own powder every third sentence.
You should add that train-platform shot you showed me at Thanksgiving. The one with the kid holding the paper bag.
Exactly. If the Times or NPR summarize the new guidance, send me that instead.
Maybe later. I like looking through those pages more than adding to them, unless I have one I have already cleaned up.
I sent you that rent calculator link. It asks about every offset and regular payment. Curious what it looks like for an older Brooklyn tenant.
Uncle Fred, the tenant group is asking people to speak Tuesday. They want older Brooklyn folks who saw the block before these rents went wild.
I can say a few words, but I will ask what happens after the speech. Who answers the phone, who checks the forms, who follows up.
Mine is plain. Rent comes straight from checking, no case number to enter, and I leave the school/car/family payment boxes empty.
That is very you lol. Bring the receipts and the clipboard.
A loud room is fine. A family getting a bad notice fixed is better.
That is wild compared with people my age. Screenshot it before you close it? I want to compare the categories.
I will send it after I block out account numbers. The only thing with a balance this month is the card, and that clears Friday.
Uncle Fred, are you coming tomorrow? Mom said you might bring something for the table.
I can bring greens and oranges. I checked three stores first because the first bunch looked tired and still rang up 3.99.
You comparison shop harder than anybody I know 😂
It keeps me from guessing. I moved a little to the reserve this morning and left the museum book for another month.
You still doing that hardware store Tuesday or did they scare you off with the stockroom?
Tuesday morning only. The nephew who runs receiving is sharp, just drowning in exception notes.
Morning only sounds civilized. After forty years we finally learned clocks have OFF switches.
The quiet afternoons are still strange. I keep pricing Kyoto hotels instead of filling every square.
You free Wednesday morning or you doing that thing by the center again?
Out from 8:20 to about 9:15 if the rain holds off. After that I can look at the schedule screenshot.
Cool. I will send it after work. You still keeping those tomato buckets alive?
Trying. They need sun more than advice from me.
Friday coffee still on? Diner has that soup again, the one that tastes like they emptied the whole shaker in it.
Still on. I will stick with eggs and toast, maybe fruit. Patel already gave me enough side-eye last week.
HA. I will not tell the waitress you are behaving.
Appreciated. I also need to swing by Walgreens after if the refill text comes through.
Uncle Freddie, for the family timeline, can I list Bed-Stuy first and then Flatbush, or am I mixing up the order?
Bed-Stuy first. Flatbush came later. There were other apartments, but no other state to put on that line.
Got it. And the document you mentioned from '62, was that city-issued or hospital-issued?
City-issued. The longer copy should show the hospital if they still print it that way.
The office had three patients today who could not get a straight answer about coverage. It wears people down.
A clinic should not feel like a maze. Same with housing forms and bus changes. People need a real person at the desk.
You always go right to the desk and the forms.
Because that is where the promise either reaches somebody or disappears.
Quick question: when you split a bill over two dates, do you get the agreement in writing?
Always. I asked the front desk to email the two payments before I sit for the crown prep.
Good. Same thing I tell my team with schedules. Paper trail.
Exactly. That is why I am keeping March plain: no new pair until the 4100 clears.
You still coming for coffee Friday? I saved that newspaper insert about Fulton Street before they tore half of it up.
Yes. Bring it. I have been going through that Moses book and a long article on delivery apps changing small storefronts.
Only you would put Robert Moses and phone delivery in the same folder.
Same streets, different machines. I will bring the clipping Ruth gave me from Weeksville too.
Tasha said you stayed on that meeting almost two hours. Please do not let those stories get you worked up before dinner.
I was fine. It just reminded me of coming home on Fulton with a receipt in my pocket and still having to account for myself.
I remember Mama making you empty your school bag before you left, just so there would be no confusion.
That is why I like clear logs now. And why I liked the part about sending the van team when somebody is unraveling on the corner.
You were quiet on the family thread. Did you call Mr. Rivera about the estimate?
Marcus said you may come by after the Knicks game. If the cousins are on the back steps again, just stay in the kitchen with me.
That is my plan. I will bring ginger ale, and maybe one beer if the score stays respectable.
No. I wrote out what to say, crossed half of it out, then found another reason to wait until Monday.
Good. I am making baked chicken, not running a lounge.
Call me after dinner instead. Remember after Mom passed, those few Thursday talks helped you get through the thick part. No shame in using a good tool twice.
Then I am safe. Text me if you need ice before the fourth quarter.
I remember. If this starts getting into my sleep or work calls, I will ask Dr. K's office what they have open.
I saw your picture from the corner near the bakery. Very moody, but I had to ask Tasha where to find it.
It was tucked in my Instagram grid. I don't put much there, so it should not be too hard to find.
You also missed two of my Facebook posts about Kayla's recital. I know you do not sit on those apps all day.
Send me the best one directly. I will look tonight after I finish sorting the contact sheet.
Tasha still trying to put you on a phone bank? She has ENERGY.
She sent a link, but I told her I am better for a ballot, a check now and then, and a conversation over coffee.
That sounds like you. Show up, do the piece you can, skip the shouting.
Exactly. Same as that one afternoon on Flatbush. I went, came home, and did not pretend I was built for every Saturday.
Fredick, did you finish the lease folder before Sunday dinner? Bring anything you want me to look over.
It is just the lease renewal, rent rider, bank copy, and the dental invoice. No office packet this year, same as last year.
Are you coming to Queens next Sunday, or do you have one of your school-gym mornings again?
Next Sunday is clear. The gym stop is later in June, but I already put the reminder in.
Good. Do not let those papers sit in a pile and worry you.
I put it in one envelope. After the card payment posts, the only open item is the dentist.
You never miss those. Bring whatever booklet you want me to look at, but no lecturing at dinner.
No lecture. Just two pages where the candidates actually answered the budget question.
I found Daddy's old program tucked in the recipe drawer. The choir names are all in that blue ink he liked.
Tasha asked me for the old church picnic names. Do you remember if the Robinsons lived over the bakery or next to the Thompsons?
Keep it for me. I can still hear his low part when the room came back on the refrain.
Next to the Thompsons. Over the bakery was the Baptiste family, and Mr. Baptiste chaired the block meeting after the blackout.
I will. And yes, before you ask, Aunt Clara's notes are in the margin about who sang too fast.
That sounds like her. Those programs tell more family history than half the official papers.
That sounds right. Mama had us in clean shirts for every meeting, even when we were just sitting in the folding chairs.
Daddy said you learn who you are by showing up, so we showed up.
Mom said Tasha is asking about Granddad again. Was he the one with the big ring of keys in that old hallway picture?
That was him. Keys on one side, flashlight on the other. He kept that building running before he came home to us.
And he was from down near Charleston, right?
Near there, yes. He did not talk much about it unless Denise or I asked at supper.
The gallery opening on Thursday has a strict RSVP. Shall I reserve two spots for us, or will Elaine be joining for old times' sake?
Reserve two for us. Elaine and I exchange the occasional hello, but that is about it now.
Understood. I will choose the 6:15 entry so you can get home before the trains thin out.
Mom said you might remember the Georgia part better than she does. Can I ask you tonight after you two talk?
Call me after 7:15. She and I usually run long when Marcus is part of the update.
Fair. Also she said the little blue-ring thing is still in her purse from last time, so stop worrying.
That is all I needed to know. Send your questions when you are ready.
Tasha says you should come for the birthday dinner Saturday. You do not have to stay late, but we want to see you.
I will come for dinner and cake. I am taking the 4:18 train and will head back after Marcus cuts the cake.
That is fine. I will save you the chair near the hallway so you can step out if the room gets too loud.
Thank you. I will bring the seltzer and the envelope for Tasha, and I will text when I get on the train.
Coffee tomorrow still good? Diner raised the omelet again. EVERYTHING IS A LUXURY NOW.
Still good. I already moved the big first-of-month line aside, so coffee survives.
Saw another older fellow from the old block packing up. Said the new papers did him in.
That is the part that stays with me. A man builds his whole week around a few corners, then a signature changes all of it.
Did the dentist finally send the bill? Please do not sit there worrying about it all evening.
It came through at $400 even. I can cover it from the bank side, but I may let Visa carry it until the consulting check clears Monday.
As long as you are not touching the long-term places for one tooth. You worked too hard setting those up.
No, those stay put. I just want the household number to stay near the six-month mark after March bills finish.
The Dumbo opening is crowded but worth it. Come early if you can; the walk from York Street has good evening shadows.
I could use the walk after sitting with receipts all afternoon. I am closing the laptop at 8:15.
Good. Bring the photo with the fruit stand reflection. And please do not answer my exhibit link from bed.
Deal. Tea only tonight; the cheddar is staying unopened.
Uncle Fredick, are you coming Sunday? Mom is making baked chicken but I can tell her not to do the heavy seasoning on yours.
I am coming. Tell her plain is fine, sauce on the side. I have been trying to keep my numbers boring.
Boring numbers are a family achievement lol. Did that March appointment go okay?
Yes. Same tiny tablet, same morning routine, and he said to send another week of readings if they creep up.
Coffee still good at 10? Or are you doing another one of those left-arm errands first?
Coffee is good. That errand was last week, and the card is back in my desk.
Smart. My cousin keeps sending me videos with miracle bottles. ALL CAPS nonsense.
Send him the city link and go drink your coffee. I am not buying health from a comment section.
Coffee still good at 2? Bring that invoice tracker if you fixed it. Mine keeps sorting names wrong.
Still good. I tested it after a YouTube walk-through this morning. The trick was locking the range before sorting.
Look at you, Chambers Street night shift paying off 40 years later.
Some of those binders still earn their shelf space. The new videos just fill in the buttons they never had then.
You still wrestling that late invoice?
Not tonight. I poured tea and put on the record with "Say It" first.
That one again. Means you are done arguing with paperwork.
Exactly. I am letting the horn take the room down a notch before I write anything back.
Are you coming Sunday? Marcus said you gave him the same lecture you gave yourself years ago.
He asked about a bigger title with no clear hours. I told him to count keys, pay, and who has his back.
Daddy would have liked that. You made a decent living by being careful, even when you took the harder store job.
Careful kept the rent paid, then the mortgage, then these little client checks. Sunday is fine; I will bring rolls.
You still meeting Calvin on 18th? I might be near there after work.
Just coffee today. I have sharp cheddar and bread waiting, plus parsley I should use before it bolts.
Understood. End of month math?
Something like that. A hot pan at home is easier than another receipt.
Mom said you had old paperwork out. You still need me to scan anything Sunday?
Maybe two pages. One has the March 12, 1962 line; the other is just old addresses.
Cool. I can make a clean PDF. You want the address page sorted by borough or by year?
By year. It reads cleaner that way, even if the train lines changed more than I did.
Mom said you might come by Queens Sunday. You still doing the call first or just coming over?
Call first, then maybe train over if my knee behaves. I already have Calvin in the morning and Ruth sent me a gallery time.
You stay booked for a man who says he does not go many places.
It is mostly the same names. That is enough for me.
Unc, when you quote those owners, do you charge by the hour or by the project?
Depends. For the three regulars I block 20 to 25 hours most weeks and bill from the notes. New one-off fixes get a flat number in writing.
Makes sense. My job has HR handling the forms, so I forget how much extra admin you do.
That extra admin is why I never spend the full deposit. A slow month can be $2,500-$3,000 before the tax money comes out.
Sent you the screenshot. The handheld says it synced, but the counts on the office computer are lower.
Look for duplicate batch numbers first. If the handheld was docked twice, it may have skipped the second file. Also compare it against the receiving sheet, not memory.
Quick work question. They want me to move two guys to nights with two days notice. Paper says supervisor discretion.
Discretion still needs a paper trail. Ask what rule they are using, put the reason in writing, and do not make the lowest-paid people absorb all the chaos.
You were right about batch 184. How do I show the boss without sounding like I am making excuses?
Make one tab: expected, scanned, posted, difference. Then a short note saying who counted and what time. Keep it plain.
You had to make those calls before?
Yes, and I learned the title on your door does not make a bad process clean. Clear rules protect everybody, including the person asked to enforce them.
The Dumbo walk is still on for Saturday. Please wear something comfortable; those cobblestones are unkind.
I will bring the older pair and keep the pace sensible. The replacement waits until April.
Sensible is acceptable. I also found a smaller opening near Atlantic if you want fewer blocks.
Atlantic is better. March already landed at 4100 after the Bay Ridge appointment deposit, so I am avoiding extra errands.
The opening tonight is still worthwhile. They added two street photographers from the old Fulton area.
I am going to pass this one. Paid for coffee, olive oil, and fruit this week, and the Lowe Street check is still sitting out there.
Understood. I will send you photographs of the strongest pieces if the room is not too crowded.
Thank you. I marked the opening fee for April and sent Lowe Street another short note after lunch.
If you photograph the finished piece, place it where the afternoon light falls across the grain. No flash.
It is not much to show off. Narrow top, two small drawers, old pulls cleaned up. But the hall finally has somewhere for keys.
That is exactly why it may photograph well. The small marks and old pulls will carry more feeling than a showroom surface.
I kept the darker scratch near the back. It was there before me, and it is not hurting anything.
Uncle Fredick, I saw your screenshot in the family chat. Are you still comparing the same two September flights? 😂
The price moved $84, and then I found a neighborhood map with better walking distances from the station.
Book the one that leaves you money for the little workshops and the photo prints. You can learn how to ask for help when you get there.
You sound like Denise. I just want mornings for gardens and side streets, not a schedule that has me chasing trains all day.
Coffee still good at 10? I can bring that little shelf bracket you wanted.
Still good. Bring the bracket, but not the long board. I have to carry everything up and the workroom is already tight.
You and that tiny shop. At least no one is moving your tools around.
True. After coffee I am filing the gas and internet confirmations, then cutting the bracket before dinner.
You survive the paddle crowd today?
Left after three games. I remembered the stretches this time, so better than last Sunday.
GOOD. Coffee Friday, unless you are limping into the diner like a tragic opera.
No opera. Just ice for a bit and one tablet with lunch if it keeps barking.
Fredick, I found another note in Mom's recipe tin. It has Aunt Pearl's name and a Sumter address on the back.
Do not toss it. I will put it with the South Carolina cards and make a clean copy for Tasha.
I will save it. For Sunday, bring the smaller pan this time. Last week everybody took home half your macaroni.
Smaller pan, and I will bring the binder tabs you wanted for the medical papers.
Mom said you found the block association flyer. Was our family always that involved?
Your grandmother did not miss much. Meetings, church suppers, school votes, rent petitions. She kept the flyers in a shoebox.
Tasha wants to frame one for the apartment. She said it explains the Burleys better than a long post.
Tell her use the 1978 one with Macon Street and the record shop ad. That is the one with our whole block in it.
If you are walking before the rain, try the bus shelter on 5th Avenue. The reflections there will be strong this morning.
I am bringing the small camera. I may take a few before coffee and decide later whether any are worth showing.
Do not let them just sit on the card. Even one posted every few weeks keeps the eye honest.
Fair. I will look tonight. I still owe Calvin a reply and there are three museum posts I saved but never opened.
Did you get outside before the rain, or are you saving your knees for tomorrow morning?
Just the corner store and a quick check on the planters. Tomorrow looks better for the Bay Ridge loop.
Good. Wear the lighter jacket, not that heavy one. And call me after if you are coming to Queens next Sunday.
Tasha asked me for Grandma's Georgia spelling again. I told her you have the church program and that little address book.
I put them in the blue folder with your school photo. Mama wrote the Georgia names in the margins.
Good. And do not leave out how she would come home tired and still line us up about homework before supper.
I remember. You got the softer look; I got the longer lecture.
Mom said you stayed after this morning because the music ran long. You good getting back?
I am fine. They stretched that last number until everybody had answered it twice. Worth the slow walk to the train.
That is the one Grandma used to hum while cooking, right?
Yes. Same tune, same lift at the end. Took me straight back to those open windows on Macon Street.

The shop is 9 to 11. I can come after lunch, as long as I do not turn the whole day into errands.

I will. The owner asked me to leave a one-page routine for his daughter before I go, so I need to finish that first.
